zh.q: 同样是从矿石里挖出来的金属，为什么有的能「烤」出来，有的只能通电？
zh.concl: 冶炼的实质是把金属从化合物里还原出来；金属越活泼，正离子越难得电子，方法就按活动性排队：K–Al 电解、Zn–Cu 热还原、Hg/Ag 热分解。
points: ① 金属在自然界主要以正价化合物（矿物）存在，少数以单质存在，要从正价变零价必须得电子。
② 金属越活泼、还原性越强，它的正离子越难得电子，就越难被还原——方法不是背的，是按活动性排出来的。
③ 所以 K、Ca、Na、Mg、Al 只能电解熔融盐，Zn→Cu 用热还原，Hg、Ag 用热分解，Pt、Au 只需物理富集。

zh.q: 焦炭能从铁矿石里把铁换出来，为什么换不出铝？
zh.concl: 铝比碳、比铁都活泼，碳还原不了氧化铝，铁也换不动铝（ΔrG° = +840.1 kJ·mol⁻¹ > 0，不自发）——所以钠、镁、铝只能电解熔融盐。
points: ① 按金属活动性顺序，铝排在碳的前面：铝的还原性比碳强，碳在工业可行的温度下还原不了 Al₂O₃。
② 把方向倒过来也不行：用铁去还原氧化铝，ΔrG° = +840.1 kJ·mol⁻¹ > 0，不自发。
③ 钠、镁、铝都靠电解熔融盐，但 NaCl 801 ℃、MgCl₂ 714 ℃ 自己熔了就导电，Al₂O₃ 要 2054 ℃ 才熔，所以必须加冰晶石把熔体温度拉下来。

zh.q: 这台槽子里面到底有什么，铝是怎么「长」出来的？
zh.concl: 电解槽就是一台电解熔融盐的装置：阳极碳块在上、阴极碳块在槽底，铝液因为比熔体重而沉在槽底，从槽底抽出。
points: ① 阳极是一排预焙碳块，从上方插进熔体；阴极碳块铺在槽底、连着槽底的钢棒。
② 中间是熔融电解质：冰晶石里溶着 2–4 % 的氧化铝，温度在 940–980 ℃。
③ 铝液密度 2.3 g/cm³ 比熔体 2.1 g/cm³ 大，所以沉在槽底，从槽底抽出去——不是「刮出来」的。

zh.q: 通了电以后，电子和离子各自往哪边走？加大电流能省电吗？
zh.concl: 阴极 Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al、阳极 2O²⁻ − 4e⁻ → O₂↑；电流越大出铝越多，但母线、导杆与熔体的欧姆压降也越大，吨铝电耗主要由槽电压和电流效率决定，不会因为电流大而省下来。
points: ① 熔体里阳离子往下走、阴离子往上走；外电路的电子由电源负极经槽底母线进来、从顶部阳极导杆回到电源正极。
② 阴极是 Al³⁺ 得电子（不是 O²⁻）；阳极放氧，氧立刻烧掉灼热的碳阳极，每千克铝要耗 0.4–0.5 kg 碳。
③ 电流越大，单位时间得电子越多、出铝越多：产量与电流成正比，300 → 400 kA 时 2.30 → 3.06 t/d。

zh.q: 氧化铝 2054 ℃ 才熔化，槽子怎么撑得住？
zh.concl: 冰晶石把 Al₂O₃ 的熔化温度从 2054 ℃ 拉到约 1000 ℃ 以下，工业电解才能在 940–980 ℃ 进行；它是熔剂，不写进总式。
points: ① 纯 Al₂O₃ 熔点 2054 ℃，直接熔了再电解，能耗和设备都撑不住。
② 冰晶石（Na₃AlF₆，熔点 1012 ℃）把氧化铝溶进去，混合熔体温度降到约 1000 ℃ 以下，工业实际工作在 940–980 ℃。
③ 冰晶石是熔剂：降低熔化温度、增加导电性，理论上不被消耗（实际有挥发损失要补加），所以不写进总反应。

zh.q: 槽温只差十几度，为什么电费差一大截？
zh.concl: 槽温降 → Al₂O₃ 溶不动、熔体电阻大 → 槽电压升 → 吨铝电耗升（955 → 940 ℃ 时 12 861 → 13 068 kW·h/t）；槽温太高虽降槽电压，但电流效率掉得更快（990 ℃ 时 0.908 → 13 111）。两头都费电，工业守在 940–980 ℃。
points: ① 槽温降低，Al₂O₃ 溶不动、熔体变黏、电阻变大，槽电压升高，吨铝电耗跟着升高：955 → 940 ℃ 时 12 861 → 13 068 kW·h/t。
② 槽温升高，槽电压是降了一点（约 3 mV/℃；低于 950 ℃ 则反过来，按 0.010/℃ 的熔体变黏项升高），但电流效率掉得更快（990 ℃ 时 η 只剩 0.908），电耗反而升到 13 111；槽衬侵蚀也加快。
③ 所以工业守在 940–980 ℃、把电耗压在 11 500–13 500 kW·h/t；教材图 8-2 给的老口径约 16 500 kW·h/t，现代槽已经降到这个区间；本课参考工况 12 861 是理论下限 8700 的 1.48 倍。

zh.q: 铝这么难弄出来，为什么还能拿它去炼铁？
zh.concl: 同一个「铝很活泼」：电解时是麻烦（必须用电硬拉），铝热时是本钱（铝把铁从氧化物里夺过来），放热 851.5 kJ·mol⁻¹、温度 2500 ℃ 以上。
points: ① 铝热里铝被氧化（0 → +3）、铁被还原（+3 → 0），铝是还原剂——方向和第 2 步完全相反。
② 反应剧烈放热（ΔrH° = −851.5 kJ·mol⁻¹），只需引燃，之后靠自身放热维持，温度可达 2500 ℃ 以上。
③ 温度超过铁熔点 1535 ℃，铁以液态流出、沉在下面，Al₂O₃ 熔渣浮在上面：可用于焊接钢轨、冶炼难熔金属。

zh.q: 产量、电耗、槽子安全同时卡着，你把这台槽调成什么样？
zh.concl: 可行域是一条二维窄带：只有槽温 950–965 ℃、电流够大又不过大时才三项同时达标——门槛是算出来的，不是背出来的。
points: ① 电耗线 ≤ 13 100 把低温那一端卡死：930 ℃ 时是 13 441 kW·h/t、935 ℃ 时 13 241，都超了。
② 产量线 ≥ 2.30 t/d 把电流下界卡在 305–310 kA；温度越高电流效率越低，越要靠加电流补产量。
③ 槽温上界 965 ℃ 卡在电流效率与槽衬安全上；越过 985 ℃ 会走「3 s 倒计时 → 槽衬蚀穿 → 事故 → 复盘 → 抢修」。

en.q: These metals all come from ores. Why can some be "baked" out while others need electricity?
en.concl: Smelting reduces the metal from its compounds; the more reactive the metal, the harder its cation gains electrons, so methods line up by reactivity: K–Al electrolysis, Zn–Cu thermal reduction, Hg/Ag thermal decomposition.
points: ① In nature most metals exist as compounds in positive oxidation states (minerals), a few as elements; going from positive to zero requires gaining electrons.
② The more reactive and reducing a metal is, the harder its cation gains electrons and the harder it is to reduce; the methods are not memorized but ranked by reactivity.
③ So K, Ca, Na, Mg and Al can only be made by electrolysis of molten salts, Zn→Cu by thermal reduction, Hg and Ag by thermal decomposition, and Pt and Au need only physical concentration.

en.q: Coke can swap iron out of iron ore. Why can't it swap out aluminum?
en.concl: Aluminum is more reactive than both carbon and iron: carbon cannot reduce alumina and iron cannot displace aluminum (ΔrG° = +840.1 kJ·mol⁻¹ > 0, not spontaneous), so sodium, magnesium and aluminum can only be made by electrolysis of molten salts.
points: ① In the reactivity series aluminum comes before carbon: aluminum is a stronger reducer, so carbon cannot reduce Al₂O₃ at industrially feasible temperatures.
② Reversing the direction does not work either: reducing alumina with iron has ΔrG° = +840.1 kJ·mol⁻¹ > 0, not spontaneous.

③ Sodium, magnesium and aluminum all rely on electrolysis of molten salts, but NaCl (801 ℃) and MgCl₂ (714 ℃) conduct once melted while Al₂O₃ melts only at 2054 ℃, so cryolite must be added to bring the melt temperature down.

en.q: What is actually inside this cell, and how does aluminum "grow"?
en.concl: The cell is an apparatus for electrolyzing molten salt: anode carbon on top, cathode carbon at the bottom, and liquid aluminum sinks to the bottom because it is heavier than the melt, where it is siphoned off.
points: ① The anode is a row of prebaked carbon blocks inserted into the melt from above; cathode carbon blocks line the bottom, connected to steel bars in the cell floor.
② In between is the molten electrolyte: 2–4 % alumina dissolved in cryolite at 940–980 ℃.
③ Liquid aluminum (2.3 g/cm³) is denser than the melt (2.1 g/cm³), so it sinks and is siphoned from the bottom, not "scraped out".

en.q: Once current flows, which way do electrons and ions go? Does more current save power?
en.concl: Cathode Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al, anode 2O²⁻ − 4e⁻ → O₂↑; more current makes more aluminum, but also bigger ohmic drops in busbars, rods and melt. Power per tonne depends mainly on cell voltage and current efficiency and is not saved by a larger current.
points: ① In the melt cations move down and anions move up; in the external circuit electrons come from the supply's negative terminal through the bottom busbar and return from the anode rods on top to the positive terminal.
② At the cathode Al³⁺ gains electrons (not O²⁻); the anode releases oxygen, which immediately burns the hot carbon anode, using 0.4–0.5 kg of carbon per kg of aluminum.
③ More current means more electrons gained per unit time and more aluminum: output is proportional to current, 2.30 → 3.06 t/d for 300 → 400 kA.

en.q: Alumina melts only at 2054 ℃. How can the cell cope?
en.concl: Cryolite brings the melting temperature of Al₂O₃ from 2054 ℃ down below about 1000 ℃, so industrial electrolysis can run at 940–980 ℃; it is a flux and is not written in the overall equation.
points: ① Pure Al₂O₃ melts at 2054 ℃; melting it directly for electrolysis would be too much for both energy and equipment.
② Cryolite (Na₃AlF₆, m.p. 1012 ℃) dissolves alumina, bringing the mixed melt below about 1000 ℃; industry actually runs at 940–980 ℃.

③ Cryolite is a flux: it lowers the melting temperature and increases conductivity, and in theory is not consumed (in practice volatilization losses are topped up), so it is not written in the overall reaction.

en.q: The cell temperature differs by only fifteen degrees. Why is the power bill so different?
en.concl: Lower cell temperature → Al₂O₃ dissolves poorly, higher melt resistance → higher cell voltage → higher power per tonne (12 861 → 13 068 kW·h/t for 955 → 940 ℃); a temperature too high lowers voltage, but current efficiency drops faster (0.908 at 990 ℃ → 13 111). Both ends waste power, so industry stays at 940–980 ℃.
points: ① Lower the cell temperature and Al₂O₃ dissolves poorly, the melt thickens and resistance rises, so cell voltage and power per tonne rise: 12 861 → 13 068 kW·h/t for 955 → 940 ℃.

② Raise the cell temperature and the voltage falls a little (about 3 mV/℃; below 950 ℃ it goes the other way via the 0.010/℃ thickening term), but current efficiency drops faster (η only 0.908 at 990 ℃), so consumption rises to 13 111, and lining erosion speeds up.

③ So industry stays at 940–980 ℃ and keeps consumption at 11 500–13 500 kW·h/t; textbook Fig. 8-2 gives an older figure of about 16 500 kW·h/t, and modern cells have come down to this range. This lesson's reference value of 12 861 is 1.48 times the theoretical minimum of 8700.

en.q: If aluminum is so hard to get out, why can it be used to make iron?
en.concl: The same "aluminum is very reactive": in electrolysis it is a nuisance (electricity must force it out), in thermite it is an asset (aluminum seizes iron's oxygen), releasing 851.5 kJ·mol⁻¹ at above 2500 ℃.
points: ① In thermite, aluminum is oxidized (0 → +3) and iron reduced (+3 → 0); aluminum is the reducing agent, exactly the opposite direction from step 2.
② The reaction is strongly exothermic (ΔrH° = −851.5 kJ·mol⁻¹); it only needs ignition, then sustains itself, reaching above 2500 ℃.
③ Above iron's 1535 ℃ melting point, iron flows out as liquid and sinks while Al₂O₃ slag floats on top: used for welding rails and smelting refractory metals.

en.q: With output, power use and cell safety all constrained, how do you set up this cell?
en.concl: The feasible region is a narrow 2D band: only at 950–965 ℃ with a current large enough but not too large are all three met; the threshold is calculated, not memorized.
points: ① The power line ≤ 13 100 shuts the low-temperature end: 13 441 kW·h/t at 930 ℃ and 13 241 at 935 ℃, both too high.
② The output line ≥ 2.30 t/d sets the lower current bound at 305–310 kA; the hotter the cell, the lower the current efficiency and the more current needed to keep output.
③ The upper temperature bound of 965 ℃ is set by current efficiency and lining safety; above 985 ℃ you get "3 s countdown → lining eroded through → accident → review → repair".
